messages:
maria: Heads-up — ran nightly perf tests, seeing a clear regression when fused RoPE scaling is enabled together with FlashAttention-v2 on paged KV mode. Baseline (no fused RoPE) median p95 token latency = 18.6ms, with fused RoPE + FA-v2 it's 26.1ms.

jin: ugh. Do you have a perf profile? sounds like a kernel selection/path explosion.

maria: Yep, attaching the quick flame snippet output and a tiny reproducer. Repro harness: small batch (B=2), max_seq=1024, kv_paging=on, rotary_dim=64, scale_factor=0.7.

maria: ```
# simplified repro settings
model = 'gptx-3b'
batch = 2
seq = 1024
rotary_dim = 64
rope_scale = 0.7
attention = FlashAttentionV2
kv_mode = paged
```

anya: Can you paste the flame percentages? where's the time going (memcpy, kernel launch, cuda sync)?

maria: top stacks: 1) kernel-dispatch overhead (22%), 2) small-kernel GEMM (18%), 3) KV page fault handling (15%), 4) rotary_apply_kernel (13%), 5) stream-sync waits (12%). Overall a bunch of short kernels now instead of one fused path.

jin: That matches my hunch — fused RoPE introduced an extra kernel that FB-v2 doesn't fuse with well, so selector splits into multiple kernels for different rotary dims. For small batches this kills throughput due to launch overhead + PCIe churn for paged KV.

tom_k: Did the selector fall back to the scalar rotary path for rotated dims not divisible by warp width? Any logs from kernel-selector?

maria: Selector log: "chosen_kernel=FA_v2_rope_split" when rotary_dim % 32 != 0 or scale_factor != 1.0. For our repro (64 dims, scale 0.7) it picks the split path.

maria: Quick numbers: B=1 p95 28ms, B=2 p95 26ms, B=8 p95 19ms (weirdly improves once batch large enough to amortize kernels).

anya: So heuristics are too binary. Maybe we should add a kernel-cost model that considers batch, seq_len, and pg/kvmode. If predicted overhead > fused path benefit, choose non-fused path or fallback to FA-v1.

jin: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: tweak kernel selector to prefer FA-v1 for paged KV when rotary_scale != 1.0 and batch <= 4. I can draft a tiny patch that checks estimated_launchs = ceil(rotary_dim/warp_width) * 2 and if launches*batch < threshold then pick v1.

maria: Works for me. Also, we could prefetch the next KV page for active streams to reduce page faults. That reduced the 15% KV stall in a quick experiment.

tom_k: Prefetch + heuristic sounds good. Any perf-bot outputs?

perf-bot: nightly/18234: fused-rope-flash: regression detected (+40% p95) on paged-kv tests. Linked job: https://ci.redwood/compare/18234

maria: Opening PR for selector heuristic + doc comment (perf/eng-infra). PR will include microbench script and threshold constants.

maria: ACTIONS: @jin to prototype selector patch, @anya to add simple cost model test in bench harness, @tom_k to validate prefetech feasibility in runtime. I'll post PR number here when ready. :thumbsup:

jin: I'll have a prototype by EOD. If it looks good we'll land behind a flag and run canary.

anya: I'll add bench cases for B in [1,2,4,8] x seq in [256,512,1024] with paged KV toggled.

tom_k: I'll check memory pressure and KMS prefetch overhead. Might need to gate prefetch by free-page count.

maria: Thanks — this should prevent user-facing regressions while we work on a proper fused kernel for the rotated/scale case.

maria: PR link: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4362 (WIP)
